clue.text: Scam entrapping Scottish smoker first succeeded, pressmen revealed

indicators.note: entrapping means one word closes round another like a snare, holding it inside

parts.note: a scam is a con
a lum is a Scottish word for a chimney, which smokes
first is written 1ST, read as IST
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A newspaper exposé reveals a fraud ensnaring a Scottish smoker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed' is only a link: the wordplay reveals the pressmen. LUM is Scottish dialect for a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Columnists write regular pieces for newspapers, so they are journalists, the press's men and women.

clue.text: Take in bread and tea maker, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that the word is to be judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: an urn is a large vessel for making tea in quantity

explanation.surface: Someone takes in bread and a tea urn, perhaps for a church fete.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, so to take in bread is to be paid wages for work.

clue.text: Shiny covering of outsize treatment centre, flash on outside

indicators.note: on outside says the word for flash is placed round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a glint is a flash of light
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a spa is a centre offering health treatments

explanation.surface: An oversized spa building gets a showy coat with a flashy exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'on outside' marks the flash word as the wrapper round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloss paint dries to a glossy finish, a shiny coat applied to surfaces.

clue.text: Petty article by this writer

parts.note: this writer is the setter referring to themself, ME
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer dismisses a short piece of their own as trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean, in the sense of small-minded or ungenerous, is a synonym of petty.

clue.text: Work in Detroit till end of October arranged

indicators.note: arranged tells the solver to put the letters into a new order
end of picks only the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A piece of writing composed in Detroit, finished by late October.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DETROIT and TILL plus R, the last letter of October, are rearranged under 'arranged'.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Dorrit is a novel by Charles Dickens, a literary work.

clue.text: Mistaken hesitation before men returned with intelligence about East

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation

indicators.note: returned means the word for men is read backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men

indicators.note: about here means the word for intelligence goes round the letter for East

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence

explanation.surface: Wrong hesitation as soldiers come back with intelligence about the East.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the crossword convention for men in the army; 'with' and 'before' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous means containing an error, so it is a synonym of mistaken or wrong.

clue.text: Observe missing Northern Ireland vehicle

indicators.note: missing tells the solver to leave the following letters out of the word

parts.note: to monitor is to observe or keep watch on

explanation.surface: An observer notes a car that is gone from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes NI out of MONITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor is an informal word for a car, a vehicle.

clue.text: One unsuccessful, solitary guy having change of heart

indicators.note: having change of heart means the central letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: a loner is a solitary person

explanation.surface: A lonely failure finally changes his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having change of heart' replaces the middle letter N of LONER with S.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who fails or does not win.

clue.text: Moved fast about present, heading off flak as result

indicators.note: about here means the word for moved fast goes round the other pieces

parts.note: tore means rushed or moved fast
here means present, as in a roll call

indicators.note: heading off takes the first letter, the head, of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone races about to deflect criticism, with consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flak' looks like part of the definition, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore means consequently, introducing something that follows as a result.

clue.text: Church home, miles away, safe place potentially

indicators.note: potentially says the letters could become something else when rearranged
away means the letter for miles is taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A home far from anywhere might serve as a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes M from HOME, leaving HOE; HOE plus SAFE and PLACE are rearranged under 'potentially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel of ease is a subsidiary church built for parishioners living far from the parish church.

clue.text: Job's time in role of king

parts.note: as means in the role of, as in acting as king
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An actor's job is a stint playing the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, a job.

clue.text: Accommodating soldiers at four in populous place shows imagination

indicators.note: accommodating means the word for a populous place holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a city is a large, heavily populated place
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Housing soldiers at four in a crowded town shows inventive thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'shows' are link words; RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Creativity is the capacity to invent and imagine, a close synonym of imagination.

clue.text: Rest area in either end of Durham

indicators.note: in places the word for either between the letters taken from Durham
end of with either picks the first or last letter of Durham

parts.note: or is the word that goes with either

explanation.surface: A place to sleep at either end of Durham, the cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'either end of Durham' as D OR M; Durham is a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dorm, short for dormitory, is a room where people sleep, an area for rest.

clue.text: Steps to cut money — very bad idea

indicators.note: to cut means one word slices into the middle of the other

parts.note: pence are British money
a stile is a set of steps over a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Building steps to save money proves a terrible plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very bad idea' is a stretch for this answer, but Collins lists an evil influence or idea as one sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilence in its figurative sense is any harmful or corrupting influence, such as a pernicious notion.

clue.text: Cautious accountant tips off granny

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: tips off picks the outer letters, the tips, of the following word

explanation.surface: A careful accountant gives a warning to an old lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips off' reads like 'warns', but it takes G and Y, the ends of granny.
explanation.definitionFit: Cagy (or cagey) means guarded and wary, reluctant to commit oneself.

clue.text: Celebrity, 51, regularly shown round

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A famous person, aged 51, is regularly escorted around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of round, O and N; 'shown' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion, as in literary lion, is a much-feted, famous person.

clue.text: Girl, one performing, about to look up — unpredicted outcome

parts.note: a miss is a girl
I is the Roman numeral one
on means performing, as in on stage
C is circa, about

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for look is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A girl on stage is about to look up and get an unexpected result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PEER into REEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Mission creep is the gradual widening of a project's aims beyond what was originally planned.

clue.text: Unsuitable hot paninis upset nurses

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read backwards
nurses means the words hold the answer within them, as a nurse holds a baby

explanation.surface: A nurse knocks over some hot sandwiches, which is unfortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' marks the run TPANI inside 'hot paninis'; 'upset' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means not appropriate or fitting, a synonym of unsuitable.

clue.text: State figure points to notice

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
N, E and S are compass points
to see is to notice

explanation.surface: A number points to a notice board.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is a state of the USA.

clue.text: Scottish city not half helping, in departure from normal

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word for the city is kept

parts.note: Aberdeen is a city in Scotland
a ration is a portion, a helping

explanation.surface: Half a Scottish city's food share is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops DEEN, the second half of ABERDEEN, leaving ABER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a deviation from what is normal or expected.

clue.text: Northeastern, he rejected bizarrely unfeasible idea

indicators.note: bizarrely tells the solver to jumble the remaining letters strangely
rejected means the letters of he are thrown out of the word

explanation.surface: A man from the north-east turns down a strange, impractical scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' removes HE from NORTHEASTERN, leaving NORTASTERN, which 'bizarrely' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-starter is a plan or proposal with no chance of success.

clue.text: Romantic set? Gorblimey, that's odd!

indicators.note: odd says the letters appear in a strange order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A film set for romance, met with an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Gorblimey is a Cockney exclamation of surprise; 'odd' rearranges it with SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Boy-meets-girl describes a conventional romantic story or plot.

clue.text: Copied theatre dialect, affected

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

indicators.note: affected means the letters are altered, put into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre imitates an affected regional accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges DIALECT into LICATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Replicated means reproduced or duplicated, a synonym of copied.

clue.text: Dad's protected by lock here, putting off outside intruder

indicators.note: protected by means the word for dad's is held safely inside the word for lock

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
pa is dad, so dad's is PA'S

indicators.note: putting off outside drops the outer letters of the word, keeping the middle

explanation.surface: A father protected by a lock keeps an intruder away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting off outside' takes the end letters off here, leaving its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespasser is someone who enters land or property without permission.

clue.text: To buy in is unpopular — sullen over costs, expensive initially

parts.note: out means unfashionable, unpopular
sour means sullen or bad-tempered

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Buying from outside is disliked, with grumbling over expensive costs.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsource is to obtain goods or services from an outside supplier rather than produce them in-house.

clue.text: Glorify former singer, last to go

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: last to go means the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an alto is a singer

explanation.surface: Praise a retired singer whose final song is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to go' drops the O from ALTO, giving ALT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt is to praise highly or raise in status.

clue.text: National uncertainty about news

indicators.note: about means the word for uncertainty is turned round

parts.note: if expresses uncertainty, as in ifs and buts
N is new, so news, in the plural, is two Ns

explanation.surface: A country feels doubt about the latest reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a native or citizen of Finland, a national of that country.

clue.text: Class output, printed

definitions.meaning: a class or kind, as in a sort of thing
to produce text, as on a typewriter or keyboard, putting it into print

explanation.definitionFit: Type means a category, and also to write with a keyboard, producing printed output.
